reason: The PR changes the ILS search policy: each new global best can trigger an additional exhaustive local-search pass before the next acceptance decision. The pinned solve entry point constructs IteratedLocalSearch, so this is a reachable solver mechanism.
solver_behavior_hypothesis: Spending more search effort whenever ILS finds a new global best may improve solution quality earlier, but can reduce iteration throughput within a fixed budget.
causal_chain: A new-best event now invokes exhaustive local search and replaces the best only if the refined candidate is feasible, changing the sequence of accepted incumbents and time spent per improvement.
structural_trigger: CVRP instances and seeds for which the ILS run discovers at least one new global best after initialization.
activation_probe: Count new-best events from solver trajectory and confirm execution of the new exhaustive-search branch with Python line coverage on a separate validation run.
instance_selection_rule: Use the fixed PyVRP CVRP development, hidden ID, and generated-shift panels with seed and budget choices frozen before reading this PR's hidden effect.
workload_exposure_plan: Run base and source-only PR images through the common PyVRP driver on CVRP instances; compare best-cost trajectories and independently verify every returned route.
mathematical_risk: An infeasible exhaustive-search result or incorrect best replacement can cause an invalid incumbent, while excessive extra search can cause resource exhaustion or missed progress.
independent_check_plan: Check original CVRP capacity, visit coverage, and objective for every solution, and run targeted ILS regression tests in both source states.
hidden_generalization_plan: Report paired hidden ID and generated-shift CVRP quality trajectories, missing runs, and per-instance regressions under unchanged budgets.
overlap_review: The source change is an ILS policy addition; compare nearby local-search PRs before counting another task from the same control path.
resource_risk: Exhaustive passes may consume most of the fixed runtime after frequent new-best events.
